issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement UML declares a constructor signature Animal(String, int) (problem_statement.md line 29), but the reference solution defines a single-argument constructor public Animal(String name) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 6) and the template Main instantiates concrete animals using a single String argument (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 9-11). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement a two-parameter constructor (name, age) or a one-parameter constructor, and will cause compilation errors if code and tests expect a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to require a single-argument constructor Animal(String) (remove age), or (B) update the template Main and the solution to implement and use a two-parameter constructor Animal(String, int) and modify all concrete animal constructors and instantiations accordingly. Ensure the UML, template examples, and reference solution use the same constructor signature so students know which constructor to implement.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for class Animal: the problem statement UML lists two attributes for Animal — name: String (problem_statement.md line 27) and age: int (problem_statement.md line 28) — but the reference solution's Animal implementation only declares a private String name field (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 4) and no age field. The template Main also constructs animals with only a name (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 9-11). This inconsistency can confuse students about required fields and whether to implement getters/setters for age.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal attributes across artifacts. Either (A) remove the age attribute from the UML/problem statement if age is not required, or (B) add an int age field to the solution's Animal class (with matching getter/setter) and update constructors and all instantiations (template Main and concrete subclasses) to accept and pass an age value. Ensure documentation, UML, template, and reference solution consistently present the same set of attributes.
